Phylogenetic diversification of the PoxtA ribosomal protection determinant
abstract: Three ATP-binding cassette subfamily F (ABC-F) PoxtA protein sequences are currently represented in NCBI's Pathogen Detection Reference Gene Catalog (WP_002415638.1, WP_209691075.1, and WP_094899500.1), while the number of publicly available sequences has steadily increased. We therefore conducted a curated survey of PoxtA homologue diversity, distribution, amino acid variability, and dissemination-associated genetic contexts. WP accessions were retrieved using BLASTp nr and a corresponding data package was obtained from NCBI Datasets v18.0.1. Proteins were aligned with MAFFT v7.525, clustered with CD-HIT v4.8.1, and maximum likelihood trees inferred in IQ-TREE v2.4.0. Gene occurrence derived from GCF assemblies containing host or source metadata. Genetic contexts were then investigated through sequence alignments of genomic regions extracted from these datasets. Among 83 non-redundant PoxtA-related WP accessions retrieved, 21 homologues clustered with canonical RefSeq PoxtA proteins, while the remaining proteins were more distantly related to ABC-F. Predominantly associated with Bacillota, homologues exhibited broad distribution across clinical, agricultural, food-associated, and environmental sources. Substitutions potentially affecting their ribosome interactions were identified mainly within the Arm subdomain and the antibiotic-resistance domain. Genomes encoding homologues exhibited diverse genetic contexts, including partial conservation of Tn6657, intact Tn6246 and Tn8026 structures, and atypical contexts carrying additional resistance genes. Homologue diversification suggests ongoing adaptation and highlights an expanding repertoire of amino acid substitutions with yet unresolved structural and functional impacts. Genetic contexts likely underlie intra- and interspecies horizontal dissemination of homologue genes by promoting co-selection under antimicrobial selective pressures.

title: Hernia, mesh, microbes, and phage promise: Mapping 35 years of evidence through a systematic review
abstract: Prosthetic mesh is the standard of care for hernia repair; however, mesh-related infections remain a significant biological challenge, with pooled data showing significant morbidity, recurrence, and elevated explantation risk. This study summarises microbiological trends documented over three decades of research, characterises the microbial landscape associated with mesh infections, and investigates how various mesh materials are associated with pathogen colonisation. The objectives are to (i) analyse the aetiology and microbial distribution in mesh-associated infections, (ii) assess the frequency of infection-related events, including mesh removal and postoperative complications, across mesh types and surgical approaches, (iii) describe study population characteristics and procedural contexts where infections occurred, (iv) identify temporal patterns in published reports, and (v) evaluate variables associated with infection-related outcomes as reported in the literature. Following PRISMA guidelines, systematic searches (1990-2025) yielded 4000 records; 584 studies met inclusion criteria, and 32 were eligible for meta-analysis, with uniform groupings by mesh type (polypropylene, biologic, composite, biosynthetic) and period (1990-2007, 2008-2025). Analytical outcomes included incisional hernia rates, surgical site infections (SSIs), explantations, and relevant patient factors, using random-effects modelling. Of the 1213 studies screened, 584 met the inclusion criteria, and 32 were included in the meta-analysis. Mesh use did not correlate with a consistent reduction of surgical site infections (HR: 0.90; p = 0.396). Mesh explantation was significantly correlated with chronic infections (HR: 6.11; p < 0.0001). Polypropylene meshes are most commonly associated with polymicrobial infections, mostly caused by S. aureus, E. coli, and P. aeruginosa. This trend may be a reporting bias, as polypropylene meshes are the most commonly used meshes worldwide. No clinical studies were found for phage-coated meshes. Preclinical evidence demonstrates the strong antimicrobial potential of phage therapy on mesh materials, but clinical efficacy has not been studied yet. The review summarises over 3 decades of hernia mesh research covering the use of mesh composition and materials, associated complications and infection management. With the rise of antibiotic resistance, bacteriophages are becoming a promising alternative for the treatment of mesh infections.

title: Associations of Urinary Triclosan Concentrations Across Gestation and Childhood with the Adolescent Gut Microbiome
abstract: Research on the influence of repeated exposure to antimicrobial chemicals, such as triclosan, on the microbiome is lacking. The goal of this study was to elucidate the associations of time-varying urinary triclosan concentrations with the adolescent gut microbiome. We used data from a prospective cohort based in Cincinnati, OH (enrolled 2003-2006, n = 146), to assess the time-varying associations of urinary triclosan concentrations with adolescent (age ∼ 12 years) gut microbiome diversity and composition. Individuals ≥ 18-years-old were recruited during the second trimester of pregnancy, and urinary triclosan concentrations were measured in pregnant women up to 2 times in pregnancy and up to 7 times in the child from ages 1 through 12 years. At age ∼ 12 years, fecal microbiome diversity and composition was characterized with metagenomic sequencing. We estimated differences in the relative abundance of prevalent (≥50%) bacterial species and gene pathways using linear regression and generalized estimating equations to assess windows of heightened susceptibility adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics. Additionally, we examined sex-specific associations by including an interaction term. The adolescent median Shannon diversity was 3.5 (IQR: 3.3, 3.5). Higher gestational triclosan concentrations with lower gut microbiome diversity [β = -0.13 per 10-fold increase (95%CI: -0.24, -0.02)]. Triclosan concentrations were also positively associated with higher abundance of antibiotic resistance genes and differential abundance of some bacterial species, with the strongest associations observed in early life and at age 12 years. We also found differences depending on sex, with more significant associations observed among males. Our findings provide insight into windows of triclosan exposure that are relevant to gut microbiome composition and the impacts of antimicrobial agents.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Microbiological Evaluation of Differently Decorated Pyrazoles Able to Overcome Antimicrobial Resistance and Biofilm Formation
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is an urgent global public health threat, killing at least 1.27 million people worldwide and associated with nearly 5 million deaths. Antibiotic resistance has been recently recognized by the WHO as a global health emergency. In this scenario, the research and development of novel derivatives specifically active against resistant pathogens became an urgent need. Pyrazole-based compounds have recently attracted significant interest for their potential antimicrobial activity, particularly against resistant Gram-positive strains such as methicillin-resistant(MRSA). Based on this evidence, we carried out an in-depth investigation of this chemical class by the synthesis of unreported compounds differently decorated on the pyrazole scaffold. The newly prepared derivatives were tested on a large panel of Gram-negative and Gram-positive strains. Interestingly, pyrazolyl ureas (PUs)andshowed excellent minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values (8-16 μg/mL) against differentstrains and were therefore further evaluated by minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) determination and time-kill assays and for their ability to inhibit biofilm formation on several MRSA strains. Pyrazolewas shown to exert such inhibition at MIC and sub-MIC concentrations (1/2 MIC and 1/4 MIC), highlighting the pharmaceutical potential of this class of compounds against resistant MRSA. Finally, selected PUs did not affect GM-6114 cell viability, thus indicating the lack of cytotoxicity on healthy fibroblasts, and were predicted to possess favorable physicochemical, pharmacokinetic, and drug-likeness profiles.

title: Integrated In silico and In Vitro Evaluation of Piperine Derivatives as Potential Efflux Pump Inhibitors in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: The increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistance mediated by efflux pump activity represents a major challenge in the treatment of infections caused by methicillin-resistant(MRSA). Efflux pumps such as NorA and MepA reduce intracellular antibiotic accumulation and contribute significantly to decreased antibiotic efficacy. In this study, PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, was evaluated as a potential efflux pump inhibitor using an integratedandapproach. Computational analysis, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Lipinski rule assessment, and ADMET prediction, was performed to investigate the interaction profiles and drug-likeness of the compound. PBSA-7 demonstrated favorable binding affinities toward NorA (-9.3 kcal/mol) and MepA (-9.0 kcal/mol), with stable interaction patterns observed during the molecular dynamics simulations. ADMET predictions suggested generally acceptable pharmacokinetic properties, although relatively high lipophilicity may require further structural optimization. Functional evaluation was performed by using checkerboard combination assays and ethidium bromide accumulation experiments. In the checkerboard assay, PBSA-7 reduced bacterial growth when combined with ciprofloxacin compared to the antibiotic alone, suggesting that the compound may enhance the antibacterial activity of ciprofloxacin against MRSA under the tested conditions. Ethidium bromide accumulation assays showed increased intracellular fluorescence, indicating potential interference with bacterial efflux pump activity. Taken together, these findings suggest that PBSA-7 may act as a potential efflux pump inhibitor associated with NorA- and MepA-mediated resistance mechanisms in MRSA, highlighting its possible role as an antibiotic adjuvant. However, further experimental studies are required to confirm the underlying mechanism and evaluate its therapeutic potential.
